questions.q: If both of them run staid campaigns attacking the other, then what percentage of students will vote in the election?
questions.solution:
Two staid issue campaigns would bring out 20 x (1+1) = 40% of students, split equally (20% each). When both attack instead, 10% of those would-be voters abstain — nothing changes hands. Turnout = 90% of 40% = 36% (D).
**Answer: 36%**
questions.shortcut: Both attacking simply shave 10% off the baseline turnout.
questions.pattern: Baseline turnout with a uniform abstention haircut
questions.passage:
Two students, Amiya and Ramya are the only candidates in an election for the position of class representative. Students will vote based on the intensity level of Amiya's and Ramya's campaigns and the type of campaigns they run. Each campaign is said to have a level of 1 if it is a staid campaign and a level of 2 if it is a vigorous campaign. Campaigns can be of two types, they can either focus on issues, or on attacking the other candidate.

If Amiya and Ramya both run campaigns focusing on issues, then
• The percentage of students voting in the election will be 20 times the sum of the levels of campaigning of the two students. For example, if Amiya and Ramya both run vigorous campaigns, then 20 × (2+2)%, that is, 80% of the students will vote in the election.
• Among voting students, the percentage of votes for each candidate will be proportional to the levels of their campaigns. For example, if Amiya runs a staid (i.e., level 1) campaign while Ramya runs a vigorous (i.e., level 2) campaign, then Amiya will receive 1/3 of the votes cast, and Ramya will receive the other 2/3.

The above-mentioned percentages change as follows if at least one of them runs a campaign attacking their opponent.
• If Amiya runs a campaign attacking Ramya and Ramya runs a campaign focusing on issues, then 10% of the students who would have otherwise voted for Amiya will vote for Ramya, and another 10% who would have otherwise voted for Amiya, will not vote at all.
• If Ramya runs a campaign attacking Amiya and Amiya runs a campaign focusing on issues, then 20% of the students who would have otherwise voted for Ramya will vote for Amiya, and another 5% who would have otherwise voted for Ramya, will not vote at all.
• If both run campaigns attacking each other, then 10% of the students who would have otherwise voted for them had they run campaigns focusing on issues, will not vote at all.

questions.q: What is the minimum percentage of students who will vote in the election?
questions.solution:
The baseline turnout 20(a+r) is smallest at 40% (both staid). Options: both attack, 10% of all would-be voters abstain, turnout 36%; only Amiya attacks, she loses 10% of her 20% (2 points), turnout 38%; only Ramya attacks, she loses 5% of her 20% (1 point), turnout 39%. Vigorous campaigns raise the baseline and cannot beat these. Minimum = 36% (B).
**Answer: 36%**
questions.shortcut: Smallest baseline is 40%; compare the abstention leak of each attacking option.

questions.q: If Amiya runs a campaign focusing on issues, then what is the maximum percentage of votes that she can get?
questions.solution:
If Ramya also focuses on issues, Amiya polls 20a at best 40%. If Ramya attacks while Amiya stays on issues, Amiya keeps her full baseline 20a and gains 20% of Ramya's baseline (which is 20r x r/(a+r) of the electorate... concretely 4r points): a=2, r=2 gives 40 + 8 = 48. Check a=2, r=1: 40 + 4 = 44; a=1, r=2: 20 + 8 = 28. Maximum = 48% (A).
**Answer: 48%**
questions.shortcut: With Amiya on issues, her votes are 20a plus 20% of Ramya's baseline (4r); push both levels to 2.
questions.pattern: Maximise a share under the attack-transfer rule

questions.q: If Ramya runs a campaign attacking Amiya, then what is the minimum percentage of votes that she is guaranteed to get?
questions.solution:
While attacking, Ramya loses 25% of her would-be votes (20% defect to Amiya, 5% abstain), keeping 0.75 x 20r x r/(a+r) = 15r^2/(a+r). If she runs staid (r=1): 7.5 against a=1, 5 against a=2. If vigorous (r=2): 20 against a=1, 15 against a=2. Her best guarantee is the vigorous campaign's worst case: 15% (A).
**Answer: 15%**
questions.shortcut: Ramya keeps 75% of her baseline when attacking; her baseline share is 20r^2/(a+r).
questions.pattern: Guarantee = minimise over the opponent's responses

questions.q: What is the maximum possible voting margin with which one of the candidates can win?
questions.solution:
Enumerate the campaign types: both on issues, the margin is |20a - 20r|, at most 20. Only Amiya attacks: Amiya 18a, Ramya 20r + 2a; best margin 42 - 18 = 24 (a=1, r=2). Only Ramya attacks: Amiya 20a + 4r, Ramya 15r; with a=2, r=1 that is 44 versus 15 — a margin of 29. Both attacking never beats these. Maximum margin = 29% (D).
**Answer: 29%**
questions.shortcut: The biggest margin has Amiya on issues (level 2) while Ramya attacks with level 1.
questions.pattern: Maximise the winning margin over all campaign combinations
